record.paper_title: Brane Supersymmetry Breaking and the Cosmological Constant: Open Problems
record.original_question: Suppose a compact brane-world model has at least two extra dimensions and admits classical solutions in which the brane vacuum energy is redirected into transverse curvature. What dynamical mechanism then selects the phenomenologically required branch with four-dimensional cosmological constant k = 0? More specifically, is bulk supersymmetry by itself sufficient to make the k = 0 solution stable once supersymmetry breaking on the brane backreacts on the bulk, and once loop corrections generate an effective potential for the modulus k, or can that potential instead have its minimum at some nonzero value of k?

evidence.quote: The issue of nearby curved solutions: it remains an open question whether supersymmetry in the bulk is good enough to ensure that the solution where all of the brane vacuum energy is absorbed in the curvature transverse (rather than parallel) to the brane is the stable one.
But in this case we still have the second problem mentioned above. There are nearby curved solutions with k 6= 0. What picks the solution with k = 0?

Even if this potential is small due to the smallness of Newton’s constant, it is not clear that the potential is such that its minimum is at k = 0. Unfortunately this remains an open problem of the scenario outlined in section 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a compact brane-world model in which our four-dimensional universe is realized as a 3-brane embedded in a higher-dimensional bulk with at least two transverse spatial dimensions. Assume the bulk theory is supersymmetric, while supersymmetry is broken on the brane, generating a brane vacuum energy of order the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Suppose the higher-dimensional Einstein equations admit a one-parameter family of static classical solutions, labeled by the four-dimensional cosmological constant k, in which the brane tension is balanced by curvature of the transverse compact dimensions; in particular, there exists a "flat" branch with k = 0 in which the brane vacuum energy is absorbed entirely into the transverse curvature, together with nearby solutions having k ≠ 0 in which the four-dimensional slices are curved (de Sitter or anti-de Sitter).

(a) Determine whether bulk supersymmetry alone is sufficient to guarantee that, once brane supersymmetry breaking backreacts on the bulk geometry, the k = 0 solution is dynamically stable within this family.

(b) Compute, or characterize qualitatively, the effective potential V(k) for the modulus k that is induced by quantum loop corrections (including those suppressed by Newton's constant), and decide whether V(k) is necessarily minimized at k = 0, or whether its minimum can lie at some k ≠ 0.

Provide a dynamical selection mechanism that singles out the phenomenologically required k = 0 branch, or else show that no such mechanism exists within the stated assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate the problem of dynamically selecting the k=0 branch among the family of nearby curved brane-world solutions, and of showing that loop-induced potentials for the modulus k are minimized at k=0, remains an open question in the literature on brane supersymmetry breaking. No subsequent work definitively resolving this selection problem was found; later contributions discuss alternative mechanisms but do not establish stability of the flat branch from bulk supersymmetry alone.

status_evidence.title: Brane Supersymmetry Breaking and the Cosmological Constant: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: It remains an open question whether supersymmetry in the bulk is good enough to ensure that the solution where all of the brane vacuum energy is absorbed in the curvature transverse is the stable one.
status_evidence.claim: The selection of k=0 among nearby curved solutions is identified as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Brane World Solution to the Cosmological Constant Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Brane vacuum energy is absorbed in transverse curvature; selection of flat slices requires additional input.
status_evidence.claim: Related proposals do not resolve the selection of the flat branch.

status_evidence.title: Vacuum Energy, Cosmological Supersymmetry Breaking and Inflation from Colliding Brane Worlds
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work explores related mechanisms but does not establish bulk SUSY suffices to stabilize k=0.
status_evidence.claim: No definitive resolution found in later literature.
